a novel series of potent renin inhibitors has been discovered.

the design and optimization of renin inhibitor 3, bearing a tertiary alcohol in a piperidine ring and an aliphatic carboxylic acid in the side chain, resulted in a potent renin inhibitor with an IC(50) = 1 nM and a K(i) = 2 nM.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel renin inhibitors, and the optimization of a series of tertiary alcohol bearing piperidines, which are potent and orally bioavailable.
the development of novel, non-peptide renin inhibitors that can be used to lower elevated blood pressure in patients.
the development of novel renin inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a combination of the right synthetic sequences and the right structural scaffolds can provide a highly effective and efficient means for identifying and optimizing a series of potent renin inhibitors.
the design of a potent, orally bioavailable, nonpeptide renin inhibitor was achieved in a relatively short amount of time.
the most potent and selective inhibitors of renin are those that are based upon a piperidine scaffold and contain a tertiary hydroxyl substituent at the 2-position.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most important structural features of the renin inhibitors are the hydrophobic interactions of the P1' side chain, and the P2 and P2' groups, which together form a "pocket" for the substrate's P1' carboxylate group.
the synthesis and optimization of the piperidine series of inhibitors was accomplished in 6 months and the optimization of the pyrrolidine series was accomplished in 3 months.
the most potent renin inhibitor identified in this series (compound 1) has an IC50 value of 0.5 nM, and a K(i) of 0.3 nM, and has a 1000-fold selectivity over ACE.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the synthesis of a large number of analogs can be accomplished in a short time frame, and that the use of a modular synthetic sequence is an effective strategy for the design and development of novel renin inhibitors.
a well-planned, iterative approach to medicinal chemistry can lead to a series of potent, efficacious, and safe compounds that can be rapidly advanced into the clinic.

, by using the appropriate synthetic tools, a diverse set of renin inhibitors can be rapidly prepared and screened in a relatively short period of time, and the results of these efforts can be used to guide the development of more potent and selective renin inhibitors.
